AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 6, 2020
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20, N-29-20, AND N-35-20, WHICH ALLOWS MEETINGS TO
VIDEOCONFERENCED WITHOUT PROVIDING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING, EITHER SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR CALL (669) 900-
6833; MEETING ID: 815 3624 5278; PASSCODE: 711010 DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK ON AN ITEM
OR UNDER ORAL COMMUNICATIONS. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR
CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-
agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  VIDEOCONFERENCE
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a):
  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles
  County Sheriff representative, and other related City officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8082-013-905; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: Department of the Air Force; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Councilmember Valencia

FLAG SALUTE
  Councilmember Rios

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to Proclaim October as Hispanic Heritage Month in the City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to Proclaim October as Paint the Town Pink, Breast Cancer Awareness Month in the City
  of Norwalk.

  III.  City Council to Proclaim October as National Community Planning Month in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Highlight of Keepin’ It Local video featuring Foodieum Cafeteria.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
 Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of
  September 15, 2020. 825-04

  Report

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period August 23, 2020 –
  September 5, 2020, in the total amount of $928.033.60. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  September 10, 2020 through September 29, 2020, in the total amount of $2,606,508.28. 640

  Report

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Irene Garcia,
  Olinda Ramirez, and Renato Verduzco. 830-07/18/22

  Report

  5.  CONFIRM EMERGENCY WORK AT 14014 ELMCROFT AVENUE – STEPHEN DORECK
  EQUIPMENT RENTALS, INC. - Staff recommends City Council confirm the emergency service line
  repair work at 14014 Elmcroft Avenue completed by Stephen Doreck Equipment Rentals, Inc., in the
  amount of $6,345.49. 955

  Report

  6.  AWARD OF CONTRACT – CREATION OF A LOCAL HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN – Staff
  recommends City Council award a contract to TetraTech in an amount not to exceed $89,769 for the
  creation of a Local Hazard Mitigation Plan; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement
  and any amendments, provided that there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. 710-03

  Report

  7.  RESOLUTION NO. 20-64 – AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER OR HIS DESIGNEE TO SIGN
  MINISTERIAL PROJECT DOCUMENTS FOR CERTAIN CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS - Staff
  recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-64, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF NORWALK, PROVIDING THE CITY MANAGER OR HIS DESIGNEE WITH BLANKET
  AUTHORITY TO EXECUTE MINISTERIAL DOCUMENTS FOR CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
  NOS. 7228, 7229, 7230, 7232, 7233, 7234, 7237, 7238, 7239, 7240, AND 7922; AND REPEALING
  RESOLUTION NO. 17-35.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  8.  ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200 RESOLUTION

  Report

REPORTS

  9.  RESOLUTION NO. 20-63 - BUDGET AMENDMENT - PROJECT NO. 7448 - AWARD OF
  CONTRACT - WELL NO. 10 EMERGENCY GENERATOR INSTALLATION PROJECT - Staff
  recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 20-63, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE FUNDS FOR PROJECT NO. 7448 - WELL NO. 10 EMERGENCY
  GENERATOR INSTALLATION, in the amount of $385,444; and
   b.  award a construction contract to Pacific Industrial Electric, in the amount of $378,240 for the Well
  No. 10 Emergency Generator Installation Project; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in
  a form approved by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7448

  Report

  10. APPROVAL OF SOLID WASTE FRANCHISE AGREEMENT AMENDMENT – Staff recommends City
  Council approve Amendment No. 1 to the Solid Waste Franchise Agreement with Athens Services; and
  authorize the Mayor to execute the amendment on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney. 1065-05-03

  Report

  11. ECONOMIC RECOVERY CODE UPDATE – Provided for City Council information. 315-01

  Report

  12. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – OCTOBER EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE - Receive
  and file this report.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated October 1, 2020.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
